subject: Different precision for random walk setting in inlabru

messages.subject: Different precision for random walk setting in inlabru
parts:
Dear discusssion community,

I am constructing a smooth function based on random walk model and spatial effect with inlabru.

My model have four variables, x, y, z, k; and I want to fit a model of y as response variable and x with second order random effect, z with 1d spatial spde random effect. The following is my code:

cmp <- y ~ fz(z, model = z.spde) + fx(x, model = "rw2")

model <- bru(components=cmp, family = "gaussian", data=data, options=list(control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-10)))

From data visualization, I notice that y highly fluctuates when k is low, so I want to set a smaller precision for the prior of the rw2 latent effect when k is less than a threshold value and a larger precision when k is greater than this threshold.

I wonder whether and how this can be achieved in inlabru function?

Many thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different precision for random walk setting in inlabru
parts:
Hi,

this is not inlabru specific, but rather applies to how to achieve
that with any inla model.

How to do it depends a bit on _how_ you would like k to affect the
model, e.g. if it's enough to have a different variance of the driving
noise for the rw2 model depending on if k is above a given value or
not, or if you want a continuous dependence on k.
It also depends on if you specifically require a rw2 model, or if some
other similar model would be ok.
But in all those cases, the easiest option I'm aware of is likely to
write your own rgeneric implementation of the model you want to have,
where you have full freedom in how k should influence the precision
matrix. You can see what the general rw2 model for irregular locations
is defined as in the Lindgren and Rue paper from 2008
(https://www.jstor.org/stable/41000297). Simpler options are to scale
the marginal distribution in a way that depends o k, but that's not
the same thing as changing the internal variability parameter of the
rw2 model, so you need to think more carefully about precisely what
model you want to have.
Finn
